questions.q: Per this lesson, why can a governance program with a well-designed operating model and policy still fail to gain adoption?
options: Because policies are always written incorrectly
Because dashboards cause people to resist governance
Because adoption is guaranteed once a policy is published
Because adoption depends on whether people actually change their daily habits, not on how well the program itself is designed
questions.explain: The lesson states adoption is a property of daily behavior change, not program design quality.

questions.q: What are the four adoption stages described in this lesson, in order?
options: Resistant, engaged, compliant, unaware
Aware, funded, mandated, retired
Compliant, engaged, unaware, resistant
Unaware, aware but resistant, compliant, engaged
questions.explain: The lesson lists this exact four-stage arc that most governance change efforts move through.

questions.q: Where does the lesson say most governance programs get stuck?
options: They oscillate randomly between all four stages
They never progress past "unaware"
They skip straight to "engaged" without any resistance
Between "aware but resistant" and "compliant" — people do the minimum because it's mandatory, not because they've bought in
questions.explain: The lesson specifically says most programs stall between resistant and compliant, producing fragile, enforcement-dependent behavior.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what is the key limitation of mandate alone?
options: Mandates only work for IT-related policies
A council can require a process but cannot mandate belief, and belief is what separates compliant from engaged
Mandates always produce full engagement immediately
Mandates are illegal in most organizations
questions.explain: The lesson draws a clear line between requiring behavior (mandate) and producing genuine buy-in (belief).

questions.q: What does "minimum viable compliance" mean in this lesson's terms?
options: A certification level for data stewards
Doing exactly enough to avoid consequences, performed under observation and abandoned once attention moves elsewhere
The smallest governance program an organization can legally run
The minimum number of policies required by regulation
questions.explain: The lesson defines this term as the behavior produced by mandate alone, without real engagement behind it.
